title: Public information trust is weakening while checking political and AI claims remains difficult
source_unit: AP-NORC State of the Facts 2026 probability-panel survey

observations.period: July 29-August 10, 2026; trust in federal government information compared with 2024

denominator.unit: percent of U.S. adults; issue-specific trust questions

inflation_cost_of_living_2026.unit: percent expressing a great deal or quite a bit of trust

inflation_cost_of_living_2024.unit: percent expressing a great deal or quite a bit of trust

health_care_2026.unit: percent expressing a great deal or quite a bit of trust

health_care_2024.unit: percent expressing a great deal or quite a bit of trust

elections_politics_2026.unit: percent expressing a great deal or quite a bit of trust

elections_politics_2024.unit: percent expressing a great deal or quite a bit of trust

reported_direction.value: declined across economy, health care, environment, jobs, abortion, and elections/politics topics

observations.method: AP-NORC comparison of 2026 and 2024 issue-specific survey estimates; the items measure trust in government information, not government performance or factual accuracy directly.
observations.uncertainty: Question wording, timing, issue salience, political context, and response composition can affect comparisons. A decline in reported trust does not establish that information became less accurate or that respondents changed behavior.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults in the AP-NORC probability-based AmeriSpeak panel; issue-specific valid bases and subgroup estimates are source-defined.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower trust may reflect institutional reputation, partisan interpretation, policy disagreement, media competition, or actual information experience; the survey does not identify which explanation dominates.

denominator.unit: percent of U.S. adults; candidate-information difficulty questions

candidate_information_true_or_not.unit: percent saying it is difficult to know whether information they encounter is true

finding_factual_candidate_information.unit: percent saying it is difficult to find factual information about candidates and positions

candidate_claims_true_or_not.unit: percent saying it is difficult to figure out whether candidates' statements are true

observations.method: Cross-sectional AP-NORC survey of perceived difficulty finding and evaluating candidate information before the 2026 midterm elections.
observations.uncertainty: These are self-reported difficulties, not an accuracy test or an observation of search time, source exposure, voting, persuasion, or turnout.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults; source summary does not provide a same-person candidate-search sequence.
observations.counterinterpretation: Difficulty may reflect information volume, low political interest, unfamiliar candidates, distrust, accessibility, or higher scrutiny rather than a single information-system failure.

denominator.unit: percent of U.S. adults; AI information and verification questions

observations.method: Cross-sectional AP-NORC survey of perceived benefits, risks, reliability, and verification of AI, chatbot, and search-result information.
observations.uncertainty: The measures are attitudes and perceived ease, not audited AI accuracy, actual use, exposure, correction attempts, or downstream decisions.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults; source summary reports national estimates and does not establish a longitudinal AI-use path.
observations.counterinterpretation: Concern can coexist with experimentation or practical use, and low confidence can reflect unfamiliarity, source differences, political context, or valid caution.

related_sources.claim: AP summary provides the same State of the Facts 2026 findings and field description.

boundary: This record shows reported trust, information-evaluation difficulty, and AI-information confidence in a cross-sectional U.S. survey. It does not establish factual accuracy, a causal decline in trust, actual candidate persuasion, voting, AI use, correction, or political action.
